text:
The fix works. The issue was in `inifile/parser.py`:
1. `line.split("=")` split on **every** `=`, so `parts[1]` only captured the segment between the first and second `=` (truncating `http://localhost:8000/?debug=1` at `?debug`).
2. `.split("#")[0]` truncated values at the first `#` (making `#ff8800` empty).

The fix splits only on the first `=` (via `split("=", 1)`) and keeps the full value, matching the module's own docstring ("split at the first `=`", "values may contain `=`, `#`, `;`"). All 3 tests pass and the exact issue scenario now returns the values as written.

arguments.summary: Fixed inifile/parser.py: replaced `line.split("=")` (which split on every `=`) with `line.split("=", 1)` so only the first `=` separates key from value, and removed the `.split("#")[0]` truncation so values containing `#` are preserved. Added an explicit `"=" not in line` check to keep the "expected...
